subject: Post-call: integration recap & backoff/idempotency plan
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Erin Zhao <erin@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: integration recap & backoff/idempotency plan

Hi Erin — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side based on the integration discussion and the questions you raised around quotas/retries/idempotency.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary use case: realtime chat + periodic batch embedding/rerank for search personalization.
- Expected traffic: bursts up to ~250 r/s at peak during onboarding, steady-state ~20 r/s.
- Constraint: Acme needs predictable tail latency; prefer client-side throttling where possible.

Integration/architecture follow-ups (what we propose)
1) SDK & auth
   - Use Redwood SDK (we provide Node/Python/Go clients). SDK has built-in token rotation and optional mTLS for private deployments.
   - Recommend API keys scoped to environment + short-lived session tokens for high-concurrency services.
2) Routing & model selection
   - Route latency-sensitive calls to the low-latency model profile; batch embedding jobs to lower-cost quantized variants.
   - We can add a routing policy that pins search rerankers to a dedicated pool to avoid noisy-neighbor interference.
3) Structured output / tool-calling
   - For tool-calling, include explicit schema and post-validate on the client. Prefer streaming + JSONL result framing for large tool outputs.
4) Embeddings & rerankers
   - Embed once on write; incremental refresh every 24h or on content-change hook. Use vector-ttl in Redis for hot items to lower token overhead.
5) Rate limiting, quotas, retries, idempotency (details below)

Rate limiting + retry guidance (recommended defaults)
- Server-side: we expose token/day quotas and concurrent request caps per API key. When limits are hit, the API returns HTTP 429 with an optional Retry-After header.
- Client-side (recommended):
   * Treat calls as: idempotent (embeddings, GET-like inference) vs non-idempotent (billing-sensitive streaming/completions).
   * For idempotent operations, retry with exponential backoff + jitter: initial 500ms, multiplier 2, max retries 5, cap backoff at 60s.
   * Honor Retry-After when present — it takes precedence over heuristic backoff.
   * For non-idempotent operations, include an idempotency key (header: X-Idempotency-Key) if you need automatic retries; otherwise, prefer client confirmation/ack before retry.
   * Always include a request identifier header (X-Request-ID) to help tracing and to enable server-side de-duplication for safe retried requests.

Operational notes
- We provide a small reference library (2 files) showing how to wire SDK retries + idempotency.
- For bulk embedding refreshes, batch calls at a controlled rate (e.g., windowed batching of 200 requests / minute) and use backpressure on the job queue if 429s start appearing.

Attachments: call-recording-20260220.mp3 (audio), acme-integration-checklist.csv (checklist).

Next steps / owners
- Dev: share a short SDK code snippet demonstrating X-Request-ID + retry behavior (due Tue 02/24).
- Jonas: follow up with sample routing config and estimated cost delta for pinned rerankers (due Fri 02/27).
- Erin: confirm embedding TTL preference and whether Acme prefers server-managed key rotation or KMS integration.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a short technical sync if the engineers want to walk through the SDK snippets.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Erin — quick technical clarifications from our infra team: 

- Concurrent limits: by default, API keys have a soft concurrent request cap of 150; this is adjustable per-account for Dedicated/Private customers (we can raise to 500 for the pilot window).
- Retry behavior: our gateway returns Retry-After on 429s for rate-based throttles. If Retry-After is present, clients MUST honor it. If not present, follow exponential backoff with full jitter. We surface a specific throttle type in the body: "throttle_type": "burst" or "throttle_type": "rate" — that can help you decide whether to slow down or pause.
- Idempotency & streaming: X-Idempotency-Key is supported for discrete API operations (embeddings, single-shot completions). For streaming sessions we recommend a session ID + resumable streaming approach — streaming resumption is supported in our SDK for Private/Dedicated customers (server-side session token + offset).
- Request IDs: include X-Request-ID on every request; we correlate logs and will suppress duplicate charge events for retried idempotent ops if the same idempotency key is seen within a 24-hour window.
- Capping retries: we recommend client-side cap of 5 retries for idempotent ops, but for low-risk reads you can keep fewer. For anything that triggers downstream state changes (billing, external hooks), avoid automatic retries unless you provide an idempotency key.
- Embedding refresh strategy: differential refresh is fine. Use a change feed (webhook) to trigger re-embedding and keep vector-ttl at ~7 days for hot items; cold items can be re-derived on demand.

Attaching a short playbook — rate-limit-playbook.md — that shows backoff code sketches (Node/Python) and server responses to watch for.

—Dev
